title.narrative: The Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) Programme

description.narrative: Australia has been working with UNDP (and FCDO UK) since 2011 to support the Government of Bangladesh (GoB) to first develop and then implement the National Social Security Strategy (NSSS) that engages over 35 ministries. Social Protection Policy Support (SPPS) program is DFAT’s partner led program that supports UNDP to provide technical assistance (TA) to GoB to implement the reform process laid out in the NSSS. DFAT's support allows a whole-of-government approach to comprehensive social security reforms. The new Social Security Policy Support Investment will be built on the progress made during 2017 to 2019 in consideration of critical lessons from the project and mid-term review of NSSS, and its subsequent revision considering COVID-19. UNDP has proposal for a period of five years (2021-2025) in two-phases: the first phase will cover 2021 to 2022; the proposed second phase will cover the remaining period.

title.narrative: The Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) Programme

description.narrative: Over the past year, the Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) Program has significantly expanded its reach and impact across Bangladesh’s social protection landscape. The program has strengthened national systems by continuing to support the development of the next-generation National Social Security Strategy (NSSS 2026+), endorsed by the Cabinet Secretary, and engaging 39 ministries in a comprehensive consultation process to improve program delivery. ‍ Key achievements include enhancement of a knowledge hub, providing policymakers with critical resources on shock-responsive and climate-resilient social protection models. The program advanced data interoperability through capacity building for MIS officials from 38 ministries, reducing fraud and optimizing resource use. A web-based M&E dashboard and roadmap for a Single Registry MIS were developed to improve monitoring and data integration. ‍ SSPS also facilitated high-level policy dialogues and consensus-building workshops, prioritizing poverty alleviation and fiscal space expansion. Research initiatives targeting urban poverty and disability-inclusive social protection frameworks aims to broaden program inclusivity. Furthermore, SSPS strengthened NGO engagement and finalized a non-state actor report to inform the NSSS chapter on marginalized groups. ‍ These efforts collectively demonstrate Australia’s pivotal role in enabling more inclusive, efficient, and resilient social protection systems that reach a broader population across Bangladesh.

The GoB considers Australia and UNDP as trusted and experienced partners in the field of social protection and requested for ongoing technical assistance and policy support to implement these reforms. SSPS is a flagship project of Cabinet Division, implemented by UNDP and focuses on providing technical and policy support to the Central Management Committee (CMC) which is the highest-level decision-making body within the government system for implementing reforms. The program has gradually extended its support to other key government agencies involved with social security reforms. SSPS Program has made significant progress towards achieving expected outcomes, including development of policy proposals for old age and disability allowances, and social insurance schemes. While GoB would provide payments to beneficiaries with or without Australia's support, the project further enhances and strengthens implementation of the reforms. In 2023, the program conducted various activities such as workshops, consultations, and pilots to advance social protection reforms.

The Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) program has delivered tangible governance reforms in Bangladesh’s social protection system. As the sole development partner directly supporting the implementation of the National Social Security Strategy (NSSS), Australia—through its collaboration with UNDP and the Cabinet Division—has played a pivotal role in driving these reforms. Over the past year, SSPS has catalyzed key reforms through technical assistance, policy guidance, and inter-ministerial collaboration, sustaining reform momentum even amid political transitions. ‍ Notable governance outcomes include improved coordination, robust monitoring systems and greater use of data in decisions. SSPS directly contributed to policy proposals for Old Age and Disability Allowances, development of the National Social Insurance Scheme, and guidelines for Shock-Responsive Social Protection. It also advanced gender-responsive policy advice and accountability tools and strengthened the influence of NGOs and OPDs in decision-making - enhancing transparency and inclusivity. ‍ Importantly, SSPS played a leading role in supporting the Local Consultative Group (LCG), a platform for structured dialogue between development partners and government agencies. This engagement has been instrumental in sustaining commitment to social protection and governance reforms. Through workshops, research, and inclusive dialogues, SSPS has empowered marginalized groups and strengthened institutional capacities for responsive, equitable, and future-ready policies.

The Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) program is a 5-year initative that provides technical assistance, policy guidance, and inter-ministerial collaboration to implement the National Social Security Strategy (NSSS). It builds on outcomes achieved through Australia’s previous social protection related efforts, which supported the successful roll-out of the NSSS, helped generate evidence and assisted in the establishment of government structures and capabilities to guide its social protection reforms. The investment works within the partner government systems which allows Australia to support the Government of Bangladesh in the primary areas of research, assessments, diagnostics, technical assistance, and policy guidance relating to social protection.
